question.:question/worked-solution:
By the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
(v(t)f(t))^{′}=v(t){f}^{′}(t)+{v}^{′}(t)f(t).
$$

Let's find ${v}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\ln{(t )}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,2 t,\,1⟩ \\ {v}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 t)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(v(t)f(t))^{′} & =v(t){f}^{′}(t)+{v}^{′}(t)f(t) \\  & =2 t⟨\frac{1}{t},\,2 t,\,1⟩+2⟨\ln{(t )},\,t^{2},\,t⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,4 t^{2},\,2 t⟩+⟨2 \ln{(t )},\,2 t^{2},\,2 t⟩ \\  & =⟨2 \ln{(t )} + 2,\,6 t^{2},\,4 t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find $(f\cdotg)^{′}(t)$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =20 t\,i- 2 t\,j+(5 t + 2)\,k \\ g(t) & =t^{3}\,i+t\,j+(t (t + 1))\,k\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$
(f\cdotg)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\cdotg(t)+f(t)\cdot{g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(20 t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5 t + 2)\,k \\  & =20\,i-2\,j+5\,k \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{3})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t (t + 1))\,k \\  & =3 t^{2}\,i+\,j+(2 t + 1)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\cdotg)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(t)\cdotg(t)+f(t)\cdot{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(20\,i-2\,j+5\,k)\cdot(t^{3}\,i+t\,j+(t (t + 1))\,k)+(20 t\,i- 2 t\,j+(5 t + 2)\,k)\cdot(3 t^{2}\,i+\,j+(2 t + 1)\,k) \\  & =((20)(t^{3})+(-2)(t)+(5)(t (t + 1)))+((20 t)(3 t^{2})+(- 2 t)(1)+(5 t + 2)(2 t + 1)) \\  & =t (20 t^{2} + 5 t + 3)+60 t^{3} + 10 t^{2} + 7 t + 2 \\  & =80 t^{3} + 15 t^{2} + 10 t + 2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
(f\cdotg)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\cdotg(t)+f(t)\cdot{g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\ln{(t )})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\,i- \frac{1}{t^{2}}\,j+\,k \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\ln{(t )})\,k \\  & =\,i- \frac{1}{t^{2}}\,j+\frac{1}{t}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\cdotg)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(t)\cdotg(t)+f(t)\cdot{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{t}\,i- \frac{1}{t^{2}}\,j+\,k)\cdot(t\,i+\frac{1}{t}\,j+\ln{(t )}\,k)+(\ln{(t )}\,i+\frac{1}{t}\,j+t\,k)\cdot(\,i- \frac{1}{t^{2}}\,j+\frac{1}{t}\,k) \\  & =((\frac{1}{t})(t)+(- \frac{1}{t^{2}})(\frac{1}{t})+(1)(\ln{(t )}))+((\ln{(t )})(1)+(\frac{1}{t})(- \frac{1}{t^{2}})+(t)(\frac{1}{t})) \\  & =\ln{(t )} + 1 - \frac{1}{t^{3}}+\ln{(t )} + 1 - \frac{1}{t^{3}} \\  & =2 \ln{(t )} + 2 - \frac{2}{t^{3}}\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
Find $(f\timesg)^{′}(t)$ where

$$
f(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 t^{2} \\ t + 4 \\ 8\end{aligned}],\,g(t)=[\begin{aligned}t + 2 \\ - 2 t^{2} \\ 5 t\end{aligned}]
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the cross product rule, we can write:

$$
(f\timesg)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\timesg(t)+f(t)\times{g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t + 4) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 t \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t + 2) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 t^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5 t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ - 4 t \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t)\timesg(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 6 t & 1 & 0 \\ t + 2 & - 2 t^{2} & 5 t\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ - 2 t^{2} & 5 t\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}6 t & 0 \\ t + 2 & 5 t\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}6 t & 1 \\ t + 2 & - 2 t^{2}\end{aligned}|k \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 t \\ - 30 t^{2} \\ - 12 t^{3} - t - 2\end{aligned}] \\ f(t)\times{g}^{′}(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3 t^{2} & t + 4 & 8 \\ 1 & - 4 t & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}t + 4 & 8 \\ - 4 t & 5\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}3 t^{2} & 8 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}3 t^{2} & t + 4 \\ 1 & - 4 t\end{aligned}|k \\  & =[\begin{aligned}37 t + 20 \\ 8 - 15 t^{2} \\ - 12 t^{3} - t - 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\timesg)^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}5 t \\ - 30 t^{2} \\ - 12 t^{3} - t - 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}37 t + 20 \\ 8 - 15 t^{2} \\ - 12 t^{3} - t - 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}42 t + 20 \\ 8 - 45 t^{2} \\ - 24 t^{3} - 2 t - 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:

$$
(f\timesg)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\timesg(t)+f(t)\times{g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6 t^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6)⟩ \\  & =⟨12 t,\,2,\,0⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4 t - 1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,6 t,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t)\timesg(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 12 t & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 t^{2} & 4 t - 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 3 t^{2} & 4 t - 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}12 t & 0 \\ 3 & 4 t - 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}12 t & 2 \\ 3 & 3 t^{2}\end{aligned}|k \\  & =⟨8 t - 2,\,12 t (1 - 4 t),\,36 t^{3} - 6⟩ \\ f(t)\times{g}^{′}(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 6 t^{2} & 2 t & 6 \\ 0 & 6 t & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 t & 6 \\ 6 t & 4\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}6 t^{2} & 6 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}6 t^{2} & 2 t \\ 0 & 6 t\end{aligned}|k \\  & =⟨- 28 t,\,- 24 t^{2},\,36 t^{3}⟩\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
Find $(f\cdotg)^{′}(t)$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =4 t\,i- 4 t\,j+(3 t + 1)\,k \\ g(t) & =t^{3}\,i+t\,j+(t (t + 1))\,k\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$
(f\cdotg)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\cdotg(t)+f(t)\cdot{g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4 t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 4 t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t + 1)\,k \\  & =4\,i-4\,j+3\,k \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{3})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t (t + 1))\,k \\  & =3 t^{2}\,i+\,j+(2 t + 1)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\cdotg)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(t)\cdotg(t)+f(t)\cdot{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(4\,i-4\,j+3\,k)\cdot(t^{3}\,i+t\,j+(t (t + 1))\,k)+(4 t\,i- 4 t\,j+(3 t + 1)\,k)\cdot(3 t^{2}\,i+\,j+(2 t + 1)\,k) \\  & =((4)(t^{3})+(-4)(t)+(3)(t (t + 1)))+((4 t)(3 t^{2})+(- 4 t)(1)+(3 t + 1)(2 t + 1)) \\  & =t (4 t^{2} + 3 t - 1)+12 t^{3} + 6 t^{2} + t + 1 \\  & =16 t^{3} + 9 t^{2} + 1\end{aligned}
$$

Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$
(f\cdotg)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\cdotg(t)+f(t)\cdot{g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5 t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t + 4)\,k \\  & =5\,i-\,j+3\,k \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{3})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t (t + 1))\,k \\  & =3 t^{2}\,i+\,j+(2 t + 1)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\cdotg)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(t)\cdotg(t)+f(t)\cdot{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(5\,i-\,j+3\,k)\cdot(t^{3}\,i+t\,j+(t (t + 1))\,k)+(5 t\,i- t\,j+(3 t + 4)\,k)\cdot(3 t^{2}\,i+\,j+(2 t + 1)\,k) \\  & =((5)(t^{3})+(-1)(t)+(3)(t (t + 1)))+((5 t)(3 t^{2})+(- t)(1)+(3 t + 4)(2 t + 1)) \\  & =t (5 t^{2} + 3 t + 2)+15 t^{3} + 6 t^{2} + 10 t + 4 \\  & =20 t^{3} + 9 t^{2} + 12 t + 4\end{aligned}

question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$
({f}^{′}\cdotf)^{′}(t)={f}^{″}(t)\cdotf(t)+{f}^{′}(t)\cdot{f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the first and second derivative of the function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2} - 1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{3} - 1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2 t,\,2,\,3 t^{2}⟩ \\ {f}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,6 t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{′}\cdotf)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{″}(t)\cdotf(t)+{f}^{′}(t)\cdot{f}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,6 t⟩\cdot⟨t^{2} - 1,\,2 t,\,t^{3} - 1⟩+⟨2 t,\,2,\,3 t^{2}⟩\cdot⟨2 t,\,2,\,3 t^{2}⟩ \\  & =((2)(t^{2} - 1)+(0)(2 t)+(6 t)(t^{3} - 1))+((2 t)(2 t)+(2)(2)+(3 t^{2})(3 t^{2})) \\  & =6 t^{4} + 2 t^{2} - 6 t - 2+9 t^{4} + 4 t^{2} + 4 \\  & =15 t^{4} + 6 t^{2} - 6 t + 2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
(f\cdotg)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\cdotg(t)+f(t)\cdot{g}^{′}(t)

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\ln{(t )})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\,i- \frac{1}{t^{2}}\,j+\,k \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\ln{(t )})\,k \\  & =\,i- \frac{1}{t^{2}}\,j+\frac{1}{t}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\cdotg)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(t)\cdotg(t)+f(t)\cdot{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{t}\,i- \frac{1}{t^{2}}\,j+\,k)\cdot(t\,i+\frac{1}{t}\,j+\ln{(t )}\,k)+(\ln{(t )}\,i+\frac{1}{t}\,j+t\,k)\cdot(\,i- \frac{1}{t^{2}}\,j+\frac{1}{t}\,k) \\  & =((\frac{1}{t})(t)+(- \frac{1}{t^{2}})(\frac{1}{t})+(1)(\ln{(t )}))+((\ln{(t )})(1)+(\frac{1}{t})(- \frac{1}{t^{2}})+(t)(\frac{1}{t})) \\  & =\ln{(t )} + 1 - \frac{1}{t^{3}}+\ln{(t )} + 1 - \frac{1}{t^{3}} \\  & =2 \ln{(t )} + 2 - \frac{2}{t^{3}}\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t)\timesg(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 6 t & 1 & 0 \\ t + 2 & - 2 t^{2} & 5 t\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ - 2 t^{2} & 5 t\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}6 t & 0 \\ t + 2 & 5 t\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}6 t & 1 \\ t + 2 & - 2 t^{2}\end{aligned}|k \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 t \\ - 30 t^{2} \\ - 12 t^{3} - t - 2\end{aligned}] \\ f(t)\times{g}^{′}(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3 t^{2} & t + 4 & 8 \\ 1 & - 4 t & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}t + 4 & 8 \\ - 4 t & 5\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}3 t^{2} & 8 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}3 t^{2} & t + 4 \\ 1 & - 4 t\end{aligned}|k \\  & =[\begin{aligned}37 t + 20 \\ 8 - 15 t^{2} \\ - 12 t^{3} - t - 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
